reviewer_independence: Independent adversarial review of committed bytes only; no builder artifact modified; no working-tree change reviewed; single new evidence file written by this review.
statement: REPRESENTATIVE SHARED-EXPERT RECOVERY SINGLE-USE RELEASE V1 REVIEW: ACCEPT. Zero blocking findings, zero non-blocking-required findings. The committed release at 6beee5cf128412e3d5bb7661be6952a01fde31a4 binds exactly the accepted shared-expert authorization and its ACCEPT review, pins the retained F_norm input and all three exact parameter payloads with dual-decoder and kernel identity enforcement before compute, closes every path to checkpoint/shard/alternate-input/routed/FFN/S2 work, pins safe machine-local paths, enforces one durable exclusive machine-wide attempt with truthful crash accounting, closes D1-D4 and retains D5 as unreachable defense-only, publishes crash-safe overwrite-proof geometry-verified output whose authority is conditional on a matching COMPLETE terminal, mandates exactly two fresh-process retained-only reproductions before COMPLETE, and preserves ledger 175 with zero checkpoint reads and zero shard opens.
composition_question: IS THIS COMMITTED SINGLE-USE RELEASE SUFFICIENT TO EXECUTE EXACTLY ONE CHECKPOINT-FREE REPRESENTATIVE SHARED-EXPERT RECOVERY WHILE AUTHORIZING NO ROUTED/SHARED COMBINATION, FFN COMPLETION, OR S2?
composition_answer: YES. The release binds by sha256 the accepted authorization (45b25de7978e01898eb5ea948202d70d5b43f33c2cbc84ec7b11a9955c5d9596), its ACCEPT review (c403c36e67a2816c6572bd2127a330a8fffa125ef4bbadd25c06db06f3b5678c), the pinned executor (d57cd1ea...), wrapper, reproducer, terminalizer, validator, tests, rehearsal, and all six contracts; every one of the 17 bindings re-hashed byte-exact at reviewed head. The wrapper reads the authorization bytes once, requires their sha256 to equal the accepted value, parses those exact bytes, and hands them to the executor, which pins the retained F_norm (687a692a452e30860c34055942061f4ff368ec0e1c815439c71e457a444fe62c, le-f32[6144], 24576 bytes), the manifest (c7669c26...), and the exact gate/up/down packed payloads (750b148a.../13727df9.../48c5469b..., 27623424 bytes total), enforces dual-decoder agreement, decoded sha256 identities (0dbb53a8.../86aae865.../97e654b6...), decoded byte counts and shapes, and decoder/kernel source identities before any shared-expert arithmetic; all identities were independently re-derived from committed bytes and live retained bytes this review. No code path in the wrapper, executor, reproducer, or terminalizer can reach a checkpoint, shard, alternate input or parameter surface, historical direct-DPREFIX output, routed aggregation, FFN completion, or S2 construction: those interfaces do not exist in the bound code, contradicting bytes fail identity gates, and the compute stops at the down projection with the stop boundary AFTER_REPRESENTATIVE_SHARED_EXPERT_OUTPUT_ONLY. Machine-wide single use is enforced by fixed non-caller-selectable paths, exclusive os.mkdir of the fixed attempt-state root, durable O_EXCL fsynced attempt-start before computation-start, durable computation-start counting the one real execution before compute regardless of outcome, permanent PRIOR_ATTEMPT refusal on any pre-existing state, and no retry/resume/second-attempt code. Publication is descriptor-relative, exclusive-temp, fsynced, no-replace hard-link, parent-fsynced, geometry- and finiteness-verified, and read back through the same directory descriptor; authority requires the matching COMPLETE release terminal, which itself requires two fresh-process retained-only reproductions with exact primary output identity. Execution remains ungated until a separate committed independent approval and an exact eight-field GO token exist; the release itself authorizes nothing (real_event_authorized false, approval_asserted false, go token verified absent on-machine).

answers.q1_binds_accepted_authorization_and_revi: YES. bindings.authorization.sha256 == 45b25de7978e01898eb5ea948202d70d5b43f33c2cbc84ec7b11a9955c5d9596 and bindings.authorization_review.sha256 == c403c36e67a2816c6572bd2127a330a8fffa125ef4bbadd25c06db06f3b5678c; both re-hashed byte-exact from committed bytes at 6beee5c; the wrapper additionally pins AUTHORIZATION_SHA as a code constant and requires the live authorization bytes to hash to it before parsing, and the validator pins both constants.
answers.q2_retained_input_and_parameters_enforce: YES. F_norm 687a692a... is the correct shared input: the bound input-vocabulary artifact and the accepted authorization bind the identical byte identity under both the routed-expert and shared-expert role names (one F_norm feeds routed and shared). The executor's OpenOnce enforces regular-file, nlink=1, no-write-bits, exact byte length, and exact sha256 before compute for the input, manifest, and all three payloads; consume() re-hashes the consumed bytes; verify_after() re-checks (dev,ino,size) and hash after compute. Dual decoders (Q5_K a/b, Q6_K a/b) must agree byte-exactly, decoded sha256 and 50331648-byte lengths must match, total packed bytes must equal 27623424, and decoder source files plus kernel implementations (strict_f32_matvec, strict_f32_silu, compute) are hash-verified against the bound computation contract before compute. All hashes independently re-derived this review from committed bytes and from the live retained files.
answers.q3_no_prohibited_path_reachable: YES. No checkpoint, shard, mmap, GGUF, routed-aggregate, FFN, residual, or S2 interface exists in the wrapper, executor, reproducer, or terminalizer (grep and full read verified). Alternate input/parameter bytes fail sha256 gates; the historical direct-DPREFIX vector has a different sha256 and cannot pass; the executor computes only gate/up/SiLU/multiply/down and returns the 24576-byte shared output. The executor's retained historical --execute CLI cannot produce alternate content (same content pins, deterministic same output) and cannot mint release authority (different terminal schema, no release binding); see finding DID-3.
answers.q4_paths_pinned_and_safe: YES. All input, parameter, attempt-state, output, approval, and go-token paths are fixed code constants matching the bound path contract; caller_selected_paths false is enforced (the wrapper accepts only the committed release path and the fixed go-token path); host home and repository root are pinned; state/output roots validated owner-only mode 0700 via O_NOFOLLOW directory descriptors. Live machine state verified this review: release root exists empty (no attempt state, no output, no go token), input and payloads retained read-only mode 0400 nlink 1 with exact hashes.
answers.q5_durable_exclusive_truthful: YES. Attempt start is exclusive (os.mkdir on the fixed root, single machine-wide winner) and durable (O_EXCL 0400 file, fsync file and directory) before computation start, which is likewise durable before compute and counts the one real execution regardless of outcome. Both begin_attempt and begin_computation sit outside the failure-terminal try-block, so a losing concurrent invocation raises without writing into the winner's state. Crash before durable attempt-start leaves the release unconsumed but permanently refused (fail-closed); crash after computation-start is reconciled by the bound read-only terminalizer as INTERRUPTED_TERMINAL_NO_RESUME with shared_expert_executions 1 and output_authority false. Retry/resume/second attempt are impossible: any pre-existing state root fails PRIOR_ATTEMPT, terminal.json is O_EXCL, and no resume code exists.
answers.q6_defense_in_depth_closeout: YES. D1: publish_no_replace creates the exclusive temp, links, and reads back all relative to one validated directory descriptor, and requires readback bytes equal to computed bytes (CONFIRMED CLOSED). D2: fixed machine-wide state and output roots, exclusive creation (CONFIRMED CLOSED). D3: the wrapper reads the authorization bytes once, hashes those exact bytes against the accepted sha, parses the same bytes, and records sha256_bytes(authorization_raw) in attempt-start (CONFIRMED CLOSED; an analogous double-read remains for approval/go-token, see finding DID-1). D4: the bound input-vocabulary artifact registers the shared-expert role alias against the identical canonical sha256 (CONFIRMED CLOSED). D5: the disagreement_role fault-injection parameter defaults to None, is never passed by the wrapper or reproducer, has no CLI plumbing in the executor's main(), and is frozen inside the hash-pinned compute implementation (CONFIRMED UNREACHABLE, DEFENSE-ONLY).
answers.q7_publication: YES. Crash-safe (temp fsync before link, parent fsync after link and after temp unlink), overwrite-proof (pre-check plus no-replace hard link that fails if the name exists; unit test verifies second publish rejected), geometry- and finiteness-verified (fstat regular/owner/mode-0400/nlink-1/size-24576, exact 6144 f32 unpack, all finite, short/long-read guards), and authority is conditional: terminal output_authority is true only for disposition COMPLETE, and the publication contract requires a matching COMPLETE terminal for any authority.
answers.q8_reproduction: YES. write_terminal refuses COMPLETE unless computation started, the output identity exists, and exactly two reproduction results are present; reproduce() runs the hash-bound reproducer twice in fresh processes with the fixed retained paths, each recomputing through the same identity-gated executor and raising unless its output sha256 equals the primary published identity; the reproducer has no checkpoint/shard/downstream interface and publishes nothing (no separate authority).
answers.q9_accounting_preserved: YES. Ledger 175 before and after (adapter gates the pinned m1f0 evidence dc53b458..., re-verified byte-exact); checkpoint reads 0 and shard opens 0 (no interface exists); exactly one future authoritative shared-expert execution counted durably at computation start; two reproduction computations separately and explicitly accounted as verification; routed aggregate executions, FFN completions, and S2 constructions fixed at zero everywhere and absent from code.
answers.q10_validator_tests_rehearsal_sufficient: YES with defense-in-depth notes. The validator pins the real producer schemas and every consequential constant (verified against actual committed artifacts, not trusted); the 39 mutation cases (10 binding, 10 output/one-shot, 10 accounting/boundary, 9 reproduction/path) all reject in repo_mode and were re-run passing this review, plus the committed-release acceptance and a live descriptor-relative publication/overwrite-rejection test; the release rehearsal exercised the real retained preflight (PRODUCTION_BINDINGS_RESOLVED, re-executed live this review with identical output), synthetic descriptor-readback publication, and links the authorization rehearsal (2/2 fresh-process exact identity, 23/23 failure cases). Gap noted as DID-4: no committed negative tests for the wrapper's approval/GO-token gate, which is exact-equality fail-closed code.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: APPROVAL_AND_GO_TOKEN_BYTES_RE_READ_ACROSS_VALIDATE_AND_RECORD
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: authorize() parses the approval via one read but computes sha256_path(approval) via a second read for the token binding, and begin_attempt() re-hashes both the approval and the go token via further reads, so a same-user swap between reads could make the recorded approval_sha256/go_token_sha256 diverge from the validated bytes. Additionally approval.reviewed_head's value is schema-required but not value-checked, and the go-token file's mode-0400/nlink-1 requirement from the path contract is not verified by the wrapper. Not exploitable across users: the approval must be committed for the clean-worktree gate, every consequential authority (release_sha256, authorization_sha256, exact token dict) is validated by content, and a same-user local attacker could equally edit any local file. Recommend the same read-once hash-then-parse pattern used for the authorization (D3 closure) in any future revision.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: LEDGER_ADAPTER_IS_LOAD_BEARING_BUT_NOT_IN_RELEASE_BINDINGS
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: scripts/research/f017_representative_expert_ledger_adapter_v1.py is imported by the wrapper and gates the ledger-175 preexecution check but is the only load-bearing file absent from the release bindings, so it is not hash-verified at execution time. Mitigations verified: it is committed at head, self-pins its evidence source (dc53b458fe9c189b4cfbfd83889e7997aa5decba799c421944ac93edb237f190, re-hashed byte-exact), any working-tree tamper fails the wrapper's clean-worktree gate, PYTHONPATH shadowing is impossible because the script directory resolves first, and every other gate (identity, single-use, publication, reproduction) is independent of the adapter. Residual risk is a head-semantics-violating future commit altering the adapter; recommend adding it to bindings in any future revision.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: HISTORICAL_EXECUTOR_CLI_EXECUTE_PATH_REMAINS_LOCALLY_INVOCABLE
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: The bound executor retains its authorization-phase --execute CLI gated only by a locally forgeable four-field token and caller-selected state/output roots. It cannot yield alternate content (input, manifest, and parameters are content-hash-pinned inside the executor, so any run computes the identical output bytes), and it cannot mint release authority (its terminal uses schema pulsarmlx.f017.representative-shared-expert-terminal without release_id/attempt_id/release_sha256, which cannot match the release terminal schema pulsarmlx.f017.representative-shared-expert-release-terminal required for authority). Worst cases are an unaccounted local shared-expert computation or pre-burning the fixed roots, which fails closed (the release wrapper then refuses forever; no false authority). The release prohibits alternate_executor and go_token_in_this_phase procedurally. Recommend that banking/consumers verify the release terminal schema and release_sha256 exactly.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: NO_COMMITTED_NEGATIVE_TESTS_FOR_APPROVAL_AND_GO_TOKEN_GATE
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: The 39 mutation cases cover the release contract via the validator, and the authorization rehearsal covered 23 executor failure cases, but no committed test exercises wrapper authorize() rejection paths (wrong verdict, wrong release_sha256, extra/missing approval keys, malformed or mismatched GO token). The gate is a chain of exact-equality require() checks over an exact key set and an exact eight-field token dict, so plausible defects fail closed; synthetic-fixture negative tests are still recommended before the approval cycle.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: INPUT_MODE_CONTRACT_STRICTER_THAN_EXECUTOR_CHECK
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: The path contract requires retained input/manifest/payload files to be MODE0400, but the executor's OpenOnce only requires no write bits (mode & 0o222 == 0, admitting e.g. 0o444), and the wrapper adds no mode check of its own. Content substitution remains impossible (exact sha256 before, at consume, and after), and the live retained files are 0400 nlink-1 (verified). Cosmetic producer/consumer divergence only.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: CRASH_BETWEEN_STATE_ROOT_MKDIR_AND_DURABLE_ATTEMPT_START_BRICKS_WITHOUT_RECORD
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: A crash after os.mkdir(state_root) but before attempt-start.json becomes durable leaves a state root with no attempt-start: the wrapper then permanently refuses (PRIOR_ATTEMPT) and the terminalizer refuses to reconcile (NO_DURABLE_ATTEMPT_START). This is fail-closed (no double attempt, no false consumption or authority, consistent with pre-attempt-failure-unconsumed semantics) but leaves no committed adjudication procedure for that narrow window. Accounting truthfulness is preserved because computation-start cannot exist in this state.
